caveats.statement: Some schools have missing or null values in the School Name column, which can cause issues when filtering or grouping by school name.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb003 WHERE cl0046 IS NULL;

caveats.statement: The Provision Type column in the school nutrition table is mostly null (82%), so queries filtering on provision type may miss many schools.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb001 WHERE cl0012 IS NULL;

caveats.statement: The Excellence Rate columns in the school performance table have many null values (26%), which can skew averages or cause missing results.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb002 WHERE cl0040 IS NULL;

caveats.statement: The Power column in the cards table uses '*' to represent no power, and also has nulls; queries must handle both cases.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb004 WHERE cl0143 = '*' OR cl0143 IS NULL;

caveats.statement: The Language column in the card foreign printing table has values like 'Portuguese (Brazil)' but queries may use 'Portuguese (Brasil)' or 'Portuguese', causing mismatches.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT DISTINCT cl0163 FROM tb005 WHERE cl0163 LIKE 'Portuguese%';

caveats.statement: The Legality Status column has values 'Legal', 'Banned', 'Restricted' but case may vary; queries using 'legal' may miss 'Legal'.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT DISTINCT cl0165 FROM tb006;

caveats.statement: The Month column in the monthly account statement table is stored as text in YYYYMM format, so date functions may not work directly.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0193 FROM tb014 LIMIT 5;

caveats.statement: The Average Monthly Balance can be negative, which may affect calculations like averages or sums if not handled.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb014 WHERE cl0198 < 0;

caveats.statement: The Weight column in the superhero table uses 0 to indicate missing weight data, which can be mistaken for a real weight of zero.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb050 WHERE cl0347 = 0;

caveats.statement: Loan status codes are not self-explanatory; 'C' means running/ok, other codes mean defaulted or finished, so filtering on status must use the code.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0229, COUNT(*) FROM tb020 GROUP BY cl0229

caveats.statement: Race lap time is stored as text in some tables and as integer milliseconds in others, so numeric comparisons need conversion.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0262 FROM tb035 WHERE cl0262 IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5

caveats.statement: Driver nationality and constructor nationality use different value sets; 'Japanese' appears in both but counts differ.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0250, COUNT(*) FROM tb025 GROUP BY cl0250 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10

caveats.statement: Event date is stored as text with time component, so YEAR() extraction requires string parsing.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0290 FROM tb036 LIMIT 5

caveats.statement: Member IDs appear in multiple formats across tables (text rec-style vs integer), so joins on member may fail.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0321 FROM tb043 LIMIT 5

caveats.statement: Circuit country values are inconsistent (e.g., 'Germany' vs 'German'), so country filters may miss rows.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT DISTINCT cl0243 FROM tb023 ORDER BY 1

caveats.statement: Qualifying rank column is stored as time text, not numeric rank, so ranking comparisons need parsing.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0278 FROM tb033 WHERE cl0278 IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5

caveats.statement: Many driver birth dates are null, so youngest/oldest queries may exclude drivers.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb025 WHERE cl0257 IS NULL

caveats.statement: Many school-level attributes (provision type, funding model, charter number) are mostly NULL, so filtering on them silently drops most schools.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(cl0012) AS provision_type_nonnull, COUNT(cl0014) AS charter_nonnull FROM tb001

caveats.statement: School IDs are stored as text and differ in format between tb001/tb003 and tb002, so joins on School ID can fail or mismatch.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb001) AS tb001_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb002) AS tb002_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb001 a JOIN tb002 b ON a.cl0001 = b.cl0030) AS matched

caveats.statement: Excellence Rate columns in tb002 are largely NULL, so averages/ratios over them cover only a subset of schools.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(cl0036) AS excellence_nonnull, COUNT(cl0040) AS excellence2_nonnull FROM tb002

caveats.statement: Card data is spread across multiple printings per Oracle ID; counting rows in tb004 counts printings, not unique cards, so distinct Oracle ID must be used for card counts.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS printings, COUNT(DISTINCT cl0160) AS unique_oracle_ids FROM tb004

caveats.statement: Power/toughness are stored as text and use '*' for variable values, so numeric comparisons on cl0143/cl0157 fail or exclude those cards.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS star_power FROM tb004 WHERE cl0143 = '*'

caveats.statement: Legality status is per format; a card can be legal in one format and banned in another, so 'banned' must always be qualified by format.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0164, cl0165, COUNT(*) FROM tb006 GROUP BY cl0164, cl0165 ORDER BY cl0164

caveats.statement: Many card attributes (flavor text, keywords, EDHRec rank) are NULL for a large share of printings, so filters on them undercount.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(cl0105) AS flavor_nonnull, COUNT(cl0101) AS edhrec_nonnull, COUNT(cl0124) AS keywords_nonnull FROM tb004

caveats.statement: Account and client IDs in the banking tables are not consistent across tables (tb013 uses Account ID/Client ID ranges that differ from tb015/tb017), so joins can lose rows.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb013) AS tx_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb013 t JOIN tb015 a ON t.cl0184 = a.cl0199) AS matched_accounts

caveats.statement: Transaction amounts in tb022 can be negative and direction is encoded separately, so summing cl0236 without filtering direction gives wrong totals.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cl0205, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(cl0236) AS min_amt, MAX(cl0236) AS max_amt FROM tb022 GROUP BY cl0205

caveats.statement: Race results are split across tb028/tb030/tb031/tb032/tb035 with overlapping Race IDs and different row grains, so joining them without dedup double-counts points.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb028) AS r28, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb030) AS r30, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb031) AS r31, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb032) AS r32, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tb035) AS r35

caveats.statement: Lap times are stored as text (e.g. '1:40.006'), so AVG/MIN on them requires parsing to seconds first.
